chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'So-and-so died and we dug a grave for him, but the earth prevented it.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'He was of bad character.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the earth refusing to accept a grave in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the metaphysical connection between moral character and the physical world, noting that the earth's refusal to accept the body was a direct consequence of the deceased's poor manners. This incident highlights the Shia emphasis on *akhlaq* (character) as a tangible spiritual reality that influences even natural elements, serving as a warning for believers to cultivate kindness and humility.
